findings.title: Docker image build downloads releases/latest, not the release being published
findings.explanation: The image is built by fetching whatever GitHub currently reports as the latest sato release, with no version argument. The publish-dockerhub job tags the same build as both 'latest' and the pushed git tag, so a rebuild of an older tag, or a release published out of order, ships a different binary than the tag name says. Every build is non-deterministic and the tag-to-binary mapping can't be audited. Holden's existing HLD_DF_008/018 findings on this line cover the insecure download itself, not this.
findings.remediation: Add an ARG VERSION to the Dockerfile and download that exact release asset. Pass it from the workflow with build-args using github.ref_name. Prefer verifying the published checksum or GPG signature after download.

findings.title: Stale workflow grants contents: write that actions/stale does not use
findings.explanation: The job requests contents: write alongside issues and pull-requests write. actions/stale only needs contents: write to delete branches, and this workflow does not set delete-branch. The token can therefore push to the repo from a job that runs daily on a schedule with a third-party action, with no benefit. Holden has no rule for this because it needs knowledge of what the action actually requires.
findings.remediation: Remove the contents: write permission from the stale job and keep issues: write and pull-requests: write.

findings.title: PR workflow 'docs' job checks out and installs Go but runs nothing
findings.explanation: The docs job has only checkout and setup-go steps and no step that generates or verifies docs. It always passes, spends a runner on every pull request and reads as though docs are being checked when they are not.
findings.remediation: Add the intended docs generation or check step, or delete the job.
